business_scope.primary_industry_name: Ownership and Cross-Border Sub-Licensing of Trademarks and Patents

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between New Zealand and Australia on Closer Economic Relations (ANZCERTA)
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP)
New Zealand–United Kingdom Free Trade Agreement
New Zealand–United States Income Tax Convention (Convention for the Avoidance of Double Taxation)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (AML/CFT Act), the AML/CFT Regulations 2011, the Companies Act 1993, the Financial Markets Authority AML/CFT Guidance, and the Reserve Bank of New Zealand / Department of Internal Affairs supervisory frameworks, together with the New Zealand Sanctions Act 2020.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copy of passport / government-issued photographic identification of each proposed director, shareholder, and beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport office or national identity authority in the applicant's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the foreign authority if the foreign state is a Hague Apostille Convention party; otherwise consular legalization at a New Zealand embassy or consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Incumbency of the parent corporate shareholder (if the beneficial owner is a body corporate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The competent company registry of the parent company's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; if the parent jurisdiction is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention, full consular legalization is required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized board resolution (or written consent of shareholders) authorizing the incorporation application and the appointment of the registered agent/secretary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the parent company or each proposed shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization in accordance with the laws of the document's state of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Professional bank reference letter or certified legal opinion confirming the identity, source of funds, and standing of each beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed commercial bank or law firm in the beneficial owner's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization and, if required by the receiving New Zealand institution, apostille or consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney and statutory declaration in favor of the New Zealand resident incorporation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, as appropriate to the foreign jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, officers, and ultimate beneficial owners against the UN Consolidated Sanctions List, the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the New Zealand Sanctions Act 2020 designated persons and entities, and the domestic New Zealand PEP register (Ministers, members of Parliament, senior public servants, judges, military officers, state-owned enterprise directors, and political party officials). Enhanced due diligence (EDD) is required for any PEP, higher-risk citizenship, or for cash-intensive or off-shore banking patterns, in accordance with AML/CFT Act sections 31-42.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office 'Companies Online' system (accessible via https://app.companiesoffice.govt.nz/companies or the New Zealand Companies Register at https://companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz/)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be expressed in Latin script (English/Māori words) and may include numbers. Names in non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into Latin characters; the transliteration must be a genuine representation and not misleading. The name must not contain characters other than basic alphanumeric forms, unless specifically authorized by the Registrar.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may file a written objection with the Companies Office Name Control section within 20 working days of the rejection notice, setting out grounds why the proposed name is not confusingly similar to an existing registered name or reserved name, and exhibiting any consent from an affected holder. If the Registrar maintains the objection, the applicant may request reconsideration by the Senior Name Review Officer. A further refusal may be appealed to the High Court of New Zealand by way of an originating application for review under the Judicature Amendment Act 1972 (or under the Companies Act 1993, section 20), and alternatively, legal title to protest can be pursued through the Part 16 'name arbitration' procedure if the objection relates to a rights infringement. Any reservation may be re-filed for an additional 20-working-day period upon payment of the statutory fee, but no automatic extension is granted.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office service is permitted for a New Zealand-incorporated international IP holding company provided the virtual office provider maintains a dedicated street address in New Zealand that is not solely a PO Box, and the provider accepts service of legal process and the Companies Office correspondence. The company must ensure its registered office and public records are accurate. For tax treaty and transfer-pricing substance purposes, a virtual office alone may not be sufficient to demonstrate management, decision-making, and genuine IP economic substance; the board should meet in New Zealand or via appropriate registrable records to mitigate thin-capitalization and permanent-establishment risk.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to moderate for a non-licensed intellectual property holding company: the Companies Office rarely makes unannounced physical inspections (estimated <5% in the first year) but the Inland Revenue Department can carry out business-intelligence visits in connection with transfer pricing, permanent establishment, or GST audits; the overall likelihood of any on-site/desk-based substance review in the first three years is approximately 15-20%, with unannounced physical site visits estimated below 5% absent specific tax or AML irregularities.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: New Zealand Companies Office name reservation and online incorporation application fee (Registrar of Companies)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the Companies Act 1993 (Companies Regulations 2020, Schedule 1)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office service (street address, document handling, statutory mail forwarding) - first calendar year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed registered office / corporate service provider in New Zealand

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT customer due diligence and UBO verification package (certified passport copies, references, sanctions/PEP screening, source-of-funds review)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: New Zealand registered law firm or corporate services provider acting as reporting entity

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and apostille / consular legalization agent fees for the mandatory document bundle (five original/four certified copies)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notaries public, competent authority in the originating jurisdiction, and/or legalization agent in the home country
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark plus statutory notarial tariffs

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company secretary / registered agent professional fee for first-year compliance and registered office representation
Commercial substance structuring and tax opinion for IP holding/patent licensing (legal profession)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: New Zealand law firm with international tax practice

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank or money-services business account opening assistance and banking AML/CFT compliance review
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: New Zealand commercial bank relationship manager or accredited introducer

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: New Zealand Companies Act 1993, primarily Sections 10 (registration of companies), 12 (requirements for incorporation), 13 (constitution), 16 (registered office), 17 (address for service), 20 (effect of registration), 122 (board powers), 128 (duties of directors), and 186 (annual return), together with Part 2 of the Companies Act 1993 and the Companies (Forms) Regulations 1994
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, an operational arm of the Ministry of Business, Innovation, and Employment (MBIE), via the New Zealand Companies Register online portal (www.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 – Application for Incorporation of a Limited Liability Company, together with Form 2 – Consent to Appointment as Director and Form 3 – Consent to Appointment as Shareholder (collectively filed as an electronic 'Register a Company' application through the Companies Office digital platform)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is required under the Companies Act 1993; an International Company may be incorporated with zero issued capital. No escrow account or bank-verified capital deposit is required for incorporation. The sole shareholder may subscribe for nominal share capital of NZD 1.00 per share, which may be credited as unpaid or fully paid at the discretion of the board without any statutory minimum.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY_NAME] LIMITED

PASSED in writing on ____ day of __________ 20___ pursuant to Section 122 and Section 91 of the Companies Act 1993

WHEREAS the Company was duly incorporated as a limited liability company under the Companies Act 1993 on ____ day of __________ 20___; and

WHEREAS the persons present as directors constitute a quorum for the transaction of business, and the board is authorized to exercise all powers of the Company.

NOW THEREFORE IT IS RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS:

1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND ALLOTMENT: RESOLVED that the Company issue and allot 1,000 ordinary shares, each of par value NZD 1.00, to the sole shareholder, [SHAREHOLDER_NAME], credited as fully paid upon the contribution of the stated consideration, and that the share register be duly recorded and the certificate of title be issued to the shareholder.

2. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company be fixed at [REGISTERED_OFFICE_ADDRESS, NEW ZEALAND], such office being situated in New Zealand, and that a copy of the Resolution and the consent of the occupier of the premises be filed and maintained in accordance with Section 16 of the Companies Act 1993.

3. APPOINTMENT OF OFFICERS: RESOLVED that [DIRECTOR_1_NAME] and [DIRECTOR_2_NAME] be, and they are hereby, appointed as the duly elected directors of the Company, with the powers and authorities conferred by the Companies Act 1993 and the Constitution; that [SECRETARY_NAME] be appointed as the Company Secretary (if applicable); and that the officers are expressly authorized to execute documents, open bank accounts, and incur expenditures necessary for the Company's incorporation and ongoing administration.

4. GOVERNANCE AND ACCOUNTING: RESOLVED that the board adopt the Company's Constitution, dated __________, as the constitutive document regulating the Company's internal governance, and that the board authorize the engagement of registered chartered accountants and legal counsel for the preparation of statutory financial statements and annual returns.

5. FURTHER AUTHORIZATION: RESOLVED that any one director or authorized officer be and is hereby empowered to file all regulatory applications, registrations, and licensing submissions necessary to conduct the Company's business as an intellectual property holding and licensing company, including tax registrations with the Inland Revenue Department.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Availability Clearance and Online Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (NZ Companies Register) and the New Zealand Intellectual Property Office (IPONZ) for trademark conflict screening via ONECheck
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a preliminary name search on the New Zealand Companies Register and ONECheck; verify that the proposed Company name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name and does not contravene the prohibited or restricted name provisions of Section 22 of the Companies Act 1993; if the name is available, reserve it for a period of up to 20 working days and record the applicant's name and reservation reference number.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name (up to 3 alternatives recommended)
Director/shareholder identification documents (passport or company extract)
Completed ONECheck inquiry reference (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is queried or rejected due to similarity, file a fresh name request with a revised corporate identifier or submit a written justification to the Companies Office for consent; appeal the decision under Section 22(4) of the Companies Act 1993 within 10 working days of the notice of refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Validation of Incorporation Dossiers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (pre-application review); licensed Director/Manager and legal counsel or registered incorporating agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the company constitution or adopt the default rules set out in the Companies Act 1993; execute consents to act as director and shareholder; confirm the registered office and address for service are physically situated in New Zealand; collate full legal names, residential addresses, and date of birth for each director and shareholder; verify that no director is disqualified under the Companies Act 1993.
required_dossiers: Form 1 – Application for Incorporation (electronic or manual)
Form 2 – Consent to Appointment as Director (signed by each proposed director)
Form 3 – Consent to Appointment as Shareholder (signed by each proposed shareholder)
Company Constitution (if opted; otherwise statutory default rules apply)
Details of registered office and address for service in New Zealand
Evidence of residential address and identity for each officer/shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application package is incomplete or inconsistent, the Companies Office will issue a deficiency notification; cure the defect by filing the corrected attestation or consent within 15 working days, failing which the application lapses and a new filing must be made with an updated fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing of Incorporation Application and Fee Payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Companies Register – online filing system)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the complete incorporation application electronically through the Companies Office 'Register a Company' portal; authenticate the filing using the RealMe login credentials of the applicant director; affirm that all directors have consented in the prescribed form; pay the official fee of NZD 150.00 (approx. USD 90.00) by credit card or online bank transfer; retain the filing receipt and transaction identification number.
required_dossiers: Complete pre-validated Form 1 application data
Authenticated director/subscriber digital signatures
Payment of official filing fee (NZD 150.00)
Constitution and consents (uploaded if electronic filing permits attachments)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office issues a query or requires further verification under Section 12(2), respond electronically through the Companies Register portal within 10 working days with the requested clarifications, re-submit any corrected schedule, and the statutory processing clock will recommence upon receipt of a complete response.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and New Zealand Business Number (NZBN)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office; New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) Register administered by MBIE
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful registration, the Companies Office will issue the Certificate of Incorporation in electronic form, evidencing the company's legal existence; an automatic NZBN will be assigned at no additional cost; verify the register entry for accuracy of the company name, registered office, shareholding, and director details; obtain the certified digital copy of the certificate for banking and licensing purposes.
required_dossiers: Filing receipt of the incorporation application
Certificate of Incorporation (issued electronically)
NZBN confirmation notice (issued automatically)
Registered office and director details as entered in the register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate of Incorporation contains clerical errors, apply to the Companies Office for rectification under Section 361 of the Companies Act 1993 with supporting administrative affidavits, and the register will be corrected without retroactive effect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting and Formalization of Corporate Governance Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the International Company
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting (physically or by unanimous written resolution) in accordance with the Constitution; adopt the pro forma first board resolution covering share capital subscription, registered office adoption, and officer appointments; issue share certificates; open the company minute book, share register, and directors' register; authorize the opening of corporate bank accounts and the execution of intellectual property assignment and licensing agreements.
required_dossiers: Notice of first board meeting
Pro forma first board resolution (as set out in the incorporation_legal_framework field)
Minutes of the first board meeting
Share certificates and share register
Consent letters of directors and officers
Bank account opening documents (certificate of incorporation, NZBN, directors' identification)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the board proceedings are challenged for quorum or notice defects, cure by convening an extraordinary general meeting or executing a subsequent unanimous written resolution confirmed by all shareholders and directors, and archive the corrective resolution with the company records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Tax Registrations and Non-Physical Occupational Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRDB); Ministry of Business, Innovation, and Employment (MBIE); local territorial authority (if any physical premise is later occupied)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply online to the Inland Revenue for an IRD number and income tax registration within the first month of activity; determine whether GST registration is required if annual turnover exceeds NZD 60,000 (or voluntarily); confirm that no physical industrial establishment is being commissioned, hence no industrial permit, environmental consent, or resource consent is triggered; if the company later rents a physical office, register with the territorial authority for building warrant of fitness and fire safety compliance.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (digital copy)
NZBN confirmation
Directors' identification documents
First board resolution confirming business activities (IP licensing) for tax registration
Registered office address confirmation for IRD correspondence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If IRD queries the ITN or GST application, file a corrective response via myIR within 20 working days; if a territorial authority later flags missing compliance sign-off, obtain a certificate of acceptance or retrospective building compliance under the Building Act 2004.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – no national industrial licensing board is mandated for an intellectual property holding and licensing company under ISIC 6420; the general administrative authority for business compliance is the New Zealand Ministry of Business, Innovation, and Employment (MBIE), and the relevant territorial local authority would have jurisdiction only if physical commercial premises are subsequently occupied.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable – the ownership and cross-border sub-licensing of trademarks and patents does not constitute a regulated industrial or professional activity in New Zealand; therefore no industry operating license, manufacturing permit, or trade-specific authorization is required. Any unrelated physical facility would require a resource consent and building compliance under the Resource Management Act 1991 and Building Act 2004.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) of New Zealand, in coordination with the local territorial authority under the Resource Management Act 1991
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – the sole operational activity is administrative/IP licensing, which produces no discharge of contaminants; no environmental impact assessment or EIA registration is required. The activity is classified as a Permitted / Non-Notified baseline administrative use under the Resource Management Act 1991. Should a physical office be established with negligible environmental footprint, a land-use consent may be required at the discretion of the territorial authority but would not trigger a full EIA.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero-discharge administrative activity; no wastewater, volatile organic compound (VOC), particulate, or hazardous waste thresholds apply. For any future physical tenancy, compliance with the National Environmental Standards for Air Quality (NES-AQ 2004), Regional Water Plan discharge limits, and Building Act 2004 Clause G4 (Ventilation) and Clause G5 (Interior Environment) would be required; all waste would be managed under the Waste Minimisation Act 2008.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No fire safety certificate, building warrant of fitness, or workplace clearance is mandatory because the company occupies no operating plant or physical premises. If and when a physical office is leased, the landlord/tenant must obtain a Building Warrant of Fitness under the Building Act 2004, a Fire Safety Compliance Certificate under the Fire and Emergency New Zealand Act 2017, and meet Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 workplace duty obligations; no special civil defense clearance is applicable to pure IP licensing.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) of New Zealand — statutory authority under the Tax Administration Act 1994. Official online portal: www.ird.govt.nz; secure filing platform: myIR. Customs interface for exports/imports: New Zealand Customs Service (www.customs.govt.nz) through the Trade Single Window (TSW).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Determine registration obligation — a non-resident International Company (CK_IC) incorporated in the Cook Islands (or another offshore centre) and managed and controlled outside New Zealand has no compulsory NZ income tax registration if it derives no New Zealand-source income and carries on no business through a permanent establishment in NZ. Step 2: If the CK_IC derives NZ-source royalty income, the NZ payer will withhold Non-Resident Withholding Tax (NRWT) at 15% (or a reduced treaty rate); registration is not strictly required solely for that passive income, but to claim treaty benefits the CK_IC must obtain an IRD number by filing Form IRD 596 (Non-Resident Company IRD Number Application) available at www.ird.govt.nz, attaching: certified certificate of incorporation, registered office address, full names and addresses of directors and shareholders, New Zealand business address details (if any), particulars of the NZ-source income, and a certificate of tax residence (IRD 595) for treaty relief. Step 3: For GST, if the CK_IC supplies remote services, electronic services, or intellectual-property licences into New Zealand and the value of those supplies to NZ consumers exceeds NZD 60,000 in any 12-month period, GST registration is compulsory; the company completes the GST section of Form IRD 596 or registers online via myIR, appoints a New Zealand address for service (an NZ tax agent is permitted but not statutorily required), and files GST returns (Form GST101) on a monthly, two-monthly, or six-monthly cycle. Step 4: The IRD issues a single 8-9 digit IRD number, which serves as the universal tax identification number for income tax, GST, NRWT, and other taxes; there is no separate VAT ID. Issuance typically takes 8-10 working days.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation / Territorial_Scope / Tax_Exempt_Zone — The CK_IC is a limited-liability company taxed at entity level; it is not a pass-through vehicle. It qualifies as a non-resident company under s YC 15 of the Income Tax Act 2007 because it is incorporated outside New Zealand and its central management and control are exercised outside New Zealand. New Zealand applies a territorial (source-based) tax system to non-residents: the CK_IC is chargeable to NZ income tax only on income with a New Zealand source (e.g., royalties paid by an NZ licensee, interest from NZ, business income attributable to a NZ fixed establishment). Its non-NZ IP sub-licensing income is wholly outside the NZ tax net. A genuine Cook Islands International Company is also statutorily exempt from Cook Islands income tax, making the vehicle a functional tax-exempt-zone entity. NZ-resident shareholders who control the CK_IC remain subject to the Controlled Foreign Company (CFC) attribution rules (s EX 20-EX 23 ITA 2007) on attributable CFC income, subject to the NZD 50,000 de minimis, but this does not alter the entity-level classification.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not operate a US-style 'check-the-box' entity classification regime; legal status follows the Companies Act 1993 and residency rules. The relevant statutory elections available to the CK_IC structure are: (1) Treaty-rate election: the CK_IC may elect to apply a reduced NRWT rate under an applicable double tax agreement by providing a certificate of tax residence (IRD 595) or by obtaining an IRD 902 exemption certificate held by the NZ payer; (2) Approved Issuer Levy (AIL) election: for interest income, the borrower may elect a 2% AIL under s 86I Stamp and Cheque Duties Act 1971 in substitution for 15% NRWT, but this election is not available for royalty payments; (3) GST grouping election: under s 55(1) GST Act 1985, NZ GST-registered entities can elect to form a GST group; the CK_IC is eligible only if it maintains NZ GST registration and does not fall within the non-resident exclusion; (4) Financial arrangements foreign-currency election: under s EW 14 ITA 2007, an election to spread foreign-currency movements using the spot-rate conversion method; (5) Hybrid mismatch elections: under subpart FH (s FH 7-FH 10) ITA 2007, the group may elect the ordering rule or the 'strongest link' rule with respect to hybrid financial instruments, hybrid entities, and imported mismatches; (6) CFC de minimis and active-business elections: NZ-resident shareholders may elect to apply the active-business test and utilise the NZD 50,000 attributable-income threshold. There is no separate 'tax-exempt-zone' election because the exemption is conferred by statute, not registration.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax — branded in New Zealand as 'Goods and Services Tax' (GST), imposed under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 (NZ) and administered by the Inland Revenue Department.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies in any 12-month period (s 51(1) GST Act 1985). A non-resident supplier of remote services or intangibles (including patent and trademark licensing) to New Zealand recipients must compulsorily register when its supplies to NZ consumers exceed NZD 60,000 per annum. Exporters making only zero-rated supplies (goods exported; services supplied to non-residents outside NZ) are not required to register, but may register voluntarily to reclaim input GST. NZ-source royalty payments received by a non-resident company are generally outside the GST system (subject to NRWT instead).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, pre-approval digital stamping, or mandatory government API invoice clearance regime exists in New Zealand. E-invoicing is voluntary and interoperable under the international Peppol PINT framework through the New Zealand e-Invoicing network, convened by the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE). GST returns (Form GST101) and NRWT schedules are filed electronically via myIR or through certified software using IRD APIs. The New Zealand Customs Service operates the Trade Single Window (TSW) with an API-based export/import declaration (CUS) and real-time customs risk screening, but this is a customs clearance mechanism, not a tax invoice clearance procedure. All tax invoices must nevertheless comply with s 24 of the GST Act 1985, requiring supplier name and GST number, recipient details, invoice date, description, GST-exclusive consideration, GST amount, and applicable rate; no machine-readable digital signature is lawfully required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods zero-rating: under s 11(1)(a) GST Act 1985, a supply of goods is zero-rated where the supplier has a contract for export and the goods are physically exported from New Zealand within 28 days of the time of supply, with the supplier retaining sufficient documentary evidence of export. Under s 11(1)(c), zero-rating applies to goods delivered outside NZ by the supplier to a non-resident recipient. Services zero-rating: under s 11A(1)(c), services supplied to a non-resident who is outside NZ at the time the services are performed are zero-rated provided the services do not relate to land in NZ or goods in NZ; for intellectual-property licensing, the rights must be for use outside New Zealand. For the CK_IC patent-licensing business, royalties paid by an NZ licensee constitute NZ-source royalties subject to 15% NRWT (or treaty-reduced rate) and are not brought into the GST system; royalties paid by foreign licensees to the CK_IC have no NZ GST nexus and require no NZ zero-rating filing. If the CK_IC physically exports goods, it must meet the 28-day export rule and the s 11 documentation requirements to claim the 0% rate and any corresponding input-tax refund.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Duly lodged New Zealand Customs export declaration (Trade Single Window 'CUS' declaration) for goods exceeding NZD 1,000 in value where not otherwise exempt
Commercial invoice for the export sale issued to the overseas buyer
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (or equivalent multimodal transport document) evidencing loading in New Zealand and discharge at an overseas port
Inward foreign-currency remittance evidence — SWIFT MT103 or bank certificate confirming receipt of export proceeds
Packing list and weight list, together with certificate of origin if preferential tariff treatment is claimed
New Zealand Customs and MPI (Ministry for Primary Industries) biosecurity clearance certificates where goods are of animal or plant origin
Copy of the underlying patent/trademark licence agreement or sale contract identifying the overseas licensee/buyer and place of use
Statutory declaration or exporter's declaration certifying physical export and destination
Proof of non-resident status of the overseas recipient (certificate of incorporation or tax residence certificate) and evidence that the licensed IP will be used outside New Zealand
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: IRD audits of zero-rated export supplies focus on physical export timing and documentation sufficiency. Goods must leave New Zealand within 28 days of the time of supply (s 11(1)(a) GST Act 1985); services must be supplied to a non-resident outside NZ and not for use in NZ (s 11A). If documentation is defective or goods are diverted to domestic consumption, IRD reassesses output tax at 15% and recovers any refund with statutory use-of-money interest under Part 7 Tax Administration Act 1994. Shortfall penalties under s 141 TAA apply as follows: 20% for failure to take reasonable care; 40% for gross carelessness or an unacceptable tax position; 100% for evasion or fraudulent intent. Late remittance penalties accrue at 1% immediately and 4% per month under s 139 TAA. Criminal prosecution is possible under ss 143A-143B TAA with substantial fines and, for individuals, imprisonment. The General Anti-Avoidance Rule (s BG 1 ITA 2007) may be invoked to dismantle artificial round-tripping structures where export proceeds are not repatriated within a commercially justifiable period — the standard trade-banking benchmark being 180 days — and transfer-pricing rules (s GC 1-GC 15 ITA 2007) may adjust cross-border IP licensing consideration. For the CK_IC, failure to substantiate the offshore use of licensed IP will expose zero-rated services to reclassification as standard-rated supplies, cumulatively assessed with interest, penalties, and clawback of all previously refunded input GST.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua); the RBNZ serves as the central bank and functional foreign-exchange administration authority for the New Zealand dollar (NZD). It issues currency, supervises registered banks and licensed non-bank deposit takers, and operates the NZClear wholesale settlement system through the Exchange Settlement Account System (ESAS). New Zealand maintains a free-floating exchange-rate regime and has no separate exchange-control board; day-to-day FX administration and cross-border payment execution are delegated to registered commercial banks. The only foreign-investment screening authority with statutory power is the Overseas Investment Office (OIO), which administers the Overseas Investment Act 2005 for acquisitions of sensitive land or significant business assets (generally 25% or more ownership interest where the consideration or asset value exceeds NZD 100 million).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand provides full current-account and capital-account convertibility: since the abolition of exchange controls in 1984, there are no Reserve Bank approvals, no currency rationing, no dual-rate tiers, and no quantitative limits on the amount or timing of inbound capital injections, outbound royalty disbursements, dividend remittances, or FX conversions for either residents or non-residents. The NZD is freely deliverable, and there are no restrictions on non-resident ownership of NZD-denominated demand or term accounts. The genuine profit-remittance hurdles are exclusively tax-based rather than FX-based: non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) at a default 15% applies to royalties and cross-border interest/dividends, with treaty-reduced rates typically ranging from 5% to 10% under applicable double-tax agreements, and the 2% approved issuer levy (AIL) may apply to certain interest-bearing obligations. For the tax-exempt-zone International Company (CK_IC), the entity's non-resident status eliminates NZ-resident income-tax exposure, and the custodial NZ banking arrangement must be documented so as not to create a New Zealand permanent establishment under the relevant double-tax treaty.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. New Zealand imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no repatriation or retention window for export receipts. Royalty, patent-licensing, and sub-licensing proceeds received by the CK_IC may be retained in NZD or any freely convertible currency, in-country or offshore, indefinitely, subject only to the source-of-funds verification and suspicious-transaction reporting obligations imposed under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 and the bank's internal FX risk limits.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account / FX Settlement Account
Capital Escrow Account / Non-Resident Foreign-Currency Account
Operational Account / Wholesale Cash Management Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-High as a supplementary rail only; not as a primary settlement channel. A licensed offshore digital EMI (e.g., Wise Business, Airwallex, or Currenxie) may operate in New Zealand subject to registration on the Financial Service Providers Register (FSPR) under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008, or may lawfully serve the IC on a wholesale-only basis, but the EMI cannot substitute for a Tier-1 RBNZ-supervised bank account because: (i) EMIs lack direct NZClear/ESAS settlement access; (ii) the IC's medium-risk-enhanced AML classification requires the capital-escrow and principal royalty-collection accounts to reside at a registered bank with an RBNZ-licensed banking licence; and (iii) outbound SWIFT MT103 disbursements to global sub-licensees are best executed through SWIFT gpi at a licensed dealer. EMI rails are therefore acceptable for pre-authorised ancillary expenses, reimbursements, and low-value operational payments, provided the EMI maintains a mirror account at a NZ clearing bank and the IC's CDD file includes the EMI's licence/registration evidence.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: New Zealand law does not impose a statutory mandate for physical appearance by directors for corporate account opening; the AML/CFT Act 2009 permits fully remote customer due diligence using accredited electronic identity verification. However, for a medium-risk-enhanced non-resident International Company without substantive domestic operations, the de facto Tier-1 bank standard requires: (i) a video-conference KYC and source-of-wealth interview with all directors and the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) of the underlying trust/proprietary structure; (ii) notarised or certified copies of the certificate of incorporation, trust deed or deed of settlement, register of directors and members, and SPF/ownership flowchart; (iii) a board resolution appointing authorised signatories; (iv) an NZ IRD number application filed through a local tax adviser; and (v) an independent legal opinion from New Zealand counsel confirming the UBO chain and the non-resident/tax-exempt-zone classification of the CK_IC. Physical appearance may be waived where the documentary trail is independently verifiable and the directors complete a live identity check at a designated overseas branch or through an accredited verification provider, but most Tier-1 banks will require at least one natural-person director or the relationship introducer to attend an in-person or branch-mediated interview.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Layered offshore trust ownership without a transparent ultimate-beneficial-owner (UBO) chain; nominee shareholding or escrowed voting rights in a Cook Islands-prototype international company is a classic enhanced due diligence trigger for non-face-to-face, non-resident entities.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Execute the full documentation bundle: (i) original or notarised trust deed/deed of settlement; (ii) IC certificate of incorporation and current certificate of good standing; (iii) complete register of members and directors with the SPF/ownership flowchart mapping every share class and voting right to named natural persons; (iv) nominee-shareholder declaration and irrevocable beneficial-ownership acknowledgement; (v) valid passports and proof of address for each UBO; and (vi) an independent legal opinion from New Zealand and Cook Islands counsel confirming the UBO under the FATF beneficial-ownership standard and the absence of any bearer-share or anonymous-ownership feature.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection materially disproportionate to the IC's stated authorised capital or paid-up capital, without a contemporaneous commercial rationale, creating a source-of-funds and round-tripping red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Assemble the transactional proof set: (i) executed global IP licensing and sub-licensing agreement; (ii) transfer-pricing benchmark study supporting the working-capital and royalty-flow requirement for the patent/trademark portfolio; (iii) board resolution authorising the equity subscription or shareholder-loan injection; (iv) source-of-funds evidence comprising 12 months of bank statements from the remitting account at a FATF-equivalent jurisdiction financial institution; and (v) the SWIFT MT103 remittance advice with a clear remittance information code stating 'Capital injection - board resolution dated [date]', together with the updated share-register and allotment forms evidencing the equity nature of the inflow.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Outbound royalty wires to high-risk jurisdictions, sanctioned entities, or inconsistent with the declared beneficial-ownership and tax-residency base, triggering sanctions-screening and correspondent-bank friction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the payment-behaviour dossier: (i) royalty computation schedules cross-referenced to audited sub-licensee income statements and the master licence agreement; (ii) certified copies of patent/trademark registration certificates evidencing the licensed IP; (iii) executed intercompany royalty agreements with arm's-length rates supported by OECD-compliant transfer-pricing documentation; (iv) NRWT settlement receipts or a certificate of residence confirming treaty-reduced withholding rates; and (v) negative-media and sanctions-clearance reports on all named beneficiary entities and settlement banks generated from Dow Jones, OFAC, UN/EU, and NZ consolidated sanctions lists, updated within the preceding 90 days.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Misclassification and substance risk: the 'Tax_Exempt_Zone' label on the CK_IC, combined with the absence of NZ-resident economic substance, triggers a dual regulatory flag under RBNZ AML/CFT supervision and IRD information-sharing protocols.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Construct the substance and status file: (i) tax-residency certificate (certificate of residence) issued by the IC's competent tax authority; (ii) IRD confirmation or tax opinion confirming that the CK_IC is treated as a non-resident company for New Zealand tax purposes; (iii) minutes of board meetings, licensing decision records, annual consolidated group transaction schedules, and a substance memorandum evidencing that IP decision-making occurs outside New Zealand; (iv) a New Zealand tax opinion confirming that mere custody of cash at a New Zealand bank and the use of NZ clearing rails do not constitute a permanent establishment under Article 5 of the applicable double-tax agreement; and (v) an AML/CFT compliance manual demonstrating ongoing monitoring, enhanced due diligence on counterparties, and periodic review triggers aligned with the medium-risk-enhanced rating.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for the CK_IC capital injection proceeds as follows: (i) the share-capital and escrow structure must be pre-approved by the relationship manager and recorded in the KYC profile; (ii) the parent or subscriber remits via SWIFT MT103 from an account at a FATF-equivalent jurisdiction bank, populating Field 70 remittance information with the code 'Capital injection - board resolution dated [date]' and Field 50K with the exact registered legal-entity name to avoid name-mismatch holds; (iii) the receiving Tier-1 NZ bank settles the inbound MT103 on a same-day basis through the SWIFT gpi channel and the NZClear Exchange Settlement Account System, crediting the Capital Escrow Account rather than the operating account where the injection exceeds the established transaction threshold; (iv) the supporting documentation package, comprising the allotment or share-issue resolution, subscription agreement, updated share register, source-of-funds statement, and board-authorised payment instruction, must be delivered before or on the next valuation day to prevent a bank-discretionary freeze; and (v) no Overseas Investment Office consent is required because the IC acquires no sensitive New Zealand land and no significant business assets. Inbound current-account items such as advance royalties are remitted under the same MT103 procedure with the purpose code 'Royalty prepayment - intercompany licence agreement' and are tagged for NRWT treatment upon maturity.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for the patent-licensing model clear through three rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 direct remittances for intercompany royalties, sub-licensee profit-share payments, and holding-company distributions, executed with a full remittance-information field referencing the underlying licence agreement, the royalty schedule, and the NRWT instruction (payable gross or under the applicable DTT rate); (ii) Commercial Letters of Credit under UCP600 and, where appropriate, URDG758 standby undertakings, used exclusively when the licensed IP is bundled with physical goods (co-branded agricultural/food shipments or patented product components) and the counterparty requires documentary trade rails; and (iii) NZClear domestic settlement channels, including direct-debit and electronic credits, for New Zealand operating expenses, trustee fees, and professional services invoices. All MT103 outbound royalty wires require an executed intercompany licence agreement, a royalty computation schedule, and source-of-funds reconciliation; disbursements above NZD 100,000 may trigger next-day enhanced due-diligence verification, and disbursements to high-risk jurisdictions are subject to the enhanced sanctions-screening protocol described in the onboarding defence dossier.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX spot contracts (NZD/USD, NZD/EUR, NZD/GBP, NZD/CNH, NZD/AUD) executed with a licensed New Zealand registered bank under the ISDA Master Agreement or a 1998 FX Master Agreement, with same-day T+2 settlement through the continuous linked settlement or bilateral correspondent bank rails.

Outright deliverable FX forwards with tenors from one month to 24 months, collateralised under a Credit Support Annex (CSA) or funded on a pre-paid basis, used to fix the NZD/USD or NZD/EUR rate on forecast royalty receivables and intercompany disbursements.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) exclusively for restricted onshore Asian currencies (CNY, TWD, INR, IDR, and other non-deliverable currencies) where onshore deliverability is legally prohibited; the NZD itself is not eligible for NDF pricing because it is a fully deliverable currency under the free-float regime.

Cross-currency swaps (NZD/USD and NZD/EUR) for converting NZD treasury cash into USD or EUR denomination to precisely match the currency profile of the IC's global royalty receivable book and third-party payment obligations, transacted under an ISDA/Schedule with a qualified licensed dealer.

FX options (vanilla European and barrier structures on EUR/USD and NZD/USD) with upfront premium payment, available to the IC as a wholesale counterparty under the derivatives-issuer licensing exemption in the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013, without retail-investor disclosure burdens.

FX swap/roll-over swaps for short-horizon liquidity management across settlement dates, subject to the IC's approved treasury policy, internal counterparty limits, and the risk-management documentation filed in the bank's KYC and onboarding record.

stage_5.statutory_deliverable: Annual Government Fee Renewal and Registered Agent Declaration (International Company annual licence renewal)
stage_5.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Cook Islands Financial Services Development Authority (Realm of New Zealand)
stage_5.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before the anniversary of incorporation, with a 30-day late-grace period recognised for online payment; due date is set on the registered agent's renewal calendar.
stage_5.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment penalty of 10% (minimum US$50) after the anniversary; failure to pay within 90 days after the anniversary or within the period specified in the Registrar's notice leads to strike-off from the International Companies Register and automatic dissolution of the company.
